title: Atlas Insurance POC sprint brief and evaluation plan
content:
Purpose: Run a focused 4-week pilot to validate Redwood Private deployed in Atlas Insurance's staging VPC for automated claims triage (first-touch summarization + intent classification + recommended next action). This brief captures scope, measurable success criteria, sprint milestones, workshop agenda, and evaluation methodology.

Background and context:
- Atlas is exploring automating initial claims intake to reduce manual routing and speed up SLA for simple claims.
- Primary constraint: PHI-like PII redaction requirements and strict network isolation. Atlas requested a Private deployment behind their VPC with customer-managed KMS.
- Goal is to prove accuracy, latency, and operational integration for 10k monthly claims volume (burst to 500/hr).

Primary objectives (what success looks like):
1) Functional correctness: Model outputs align with Atlas triage rubric (classification + short summary + recommended action) for >= 85% of sampled claims by weighted F1.
2) Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end (API arrival -> response) <= 800ms for typical payloads (claim text <= 1,200 tokens).
3) Throughput: Dedicated pool can sustain 400 concurrent requests with average latency <= 1s and CPU/GPU usage within planned headroom.
4) Security & compliance: Deployment uses Atlas KMS keys, audit logs forwarded to Atlas SIEM, and no unencrypted logs leave the VPC.
5) Integration: Auto-routing results written to Atlas staging queue (SQS) and recorded in their claims audit table.
6) Business impact signal: Human-in-the-loop reviewers accept Redwood-assisted decisions without edit in >= 70% of reviewed cases during the pilot sampling.

Out of scope:
- Full production hardening (SLA contract) — this is a pilot only.
- Complex downstream automations beyond routing (no automatic payouts).
- Retraining Atlas proprietary models — only inference & light prompt-based adaptation.

Acceptance criteria (pass/fail gates):
- Functional gate: Weighted F1 >= 0.85 on evaluation set of 1,000 labeled historical claims (stratified across channels: email, form, phone transcript).
- Latency gate: p95 <= 800ms for 80% of load tests and p95 <= 1.2s under burst test (500 rps sustained for 5 min).
- Security gate: KMS integration verified, VPC egress rules validated by Atlas security, and audit logs present for 100% of requests during a 24h verification window.
- Integration gate: Successful end-to-end flow for the canonical pipeline (ingest -> infer -> SQS -> audit) in staging environment.
- UX gate: In a blind review of 200 model-assisted triaged claims, 70% or more are accepted by human reviewers without modification.

Metrics to track (dashboard items):
- Model quality: Precision, recall, F1 per intent class; summary ROUGE-L against gold summaries; calibration (confidence vs accuracy).
- Latency: p50/p90/p95 for end-to-end and model-only inference token loop.
- Throughput: requests/sec sustained, concurrency, average GPU utilization, OOM/retry events.
- Cost signal: tokens per request, avg inference compute time, approximate cost per 1k requests (pilot estimate).
- Operational: error rate (4xx, 5xx), cold-starts, cache hit rate for prefix cache.
- Business: human accept rate, median time to triage (human vs assisted).

Sprint timeline (4 weeks)
Week 0 (Pre-kick): Security onboarding, account and VPC peering, KMS exchange, test credentials.
Week 1: Minimal deploy + sanity tests
- Deploy Redwood Private control plane connector and inference nodes in Atlas staging VPC (small pool).
- Run smoke tests (connectivity, simple inference, KMS ops).
- Workshop #1 (Day 3): Integration checklist walk-through with Atlas eng + security.
Week 2: Integration and sample data runs
- Ingest 1k historical claims (anonymized) through staging pipeline.
- Iterate prompt templates for classification and summary length constraints.
- Run automated evaluation on held-out labels.
Week 3: Load and resilience tests
- Scale to target throughput, run burst tests, observe p95 behavior.
- Introduce synthetic noise (typos, transcripts) to validate robustness.
- Workshop #2 (mid-week): Review quality metrics, adjust batching and quantization profile suggestions.
Week 4: Acceptance window and handover
- Run final 24h verification (security + audit + integration).
- Collect blind human-review sample and compute acceptance metrics.
- Debrief session with Atlas to review results and next steps.

Workshop agenda (initial kickoff & integration):
- Duration: 90 minutes (Day 1–3 of Week 1)
- Goals: confirm roles, network/credentials, success criteria, and immediate next steps
- Agenda:
  1) Introductions & objectives (10 min)
  2) Architecture overview: Redwood Private in Atlas VPC (10 min)
  3) Data flow & redaction strategy (15 min)
  4) Integration points: SQS, audit DB, SIEM (15 min)
  5) Acceptance criteria & evaluation plan (20 min)
  6) Open issues, risks, immediate blockers (15 min)
  7) Actions & owners (5 min)

Technical checklist (pre-deploy validations):
- VPC peering/firewall rules allow internal control plane traffic on required ports.
- Atlas KMS key ARN provided and test encrypt/decrypt cycle completed.
- Staging SQS queue URL & IAM role for write access configured.
- SIEM webhook endpoint or S3 sink available and write permissions validated.
- Historical claim dataset (CSV/JSON) with PII redaction script provided (sample schema).
- Observability hooks enabled: token-level tracing, per-request ids, logs to stdout disabled; structured audit logs to SIEM only.
- SLOs configured in Redwood Console for p95 latency and error budget alerts.

Prompt engineering notes (starting templates):
- Classification prompt (instruction + few-shot): classify intent into [billing_query, policy_update, small_claim, large_claim, other], return single label and confidence. Keep instruction explicit about labels.
- Summary prompt: "Produce a 1-2 sentence summary of the claimant's issue focusing on resolution action and key metadata (policy id, date, incident)." Limit to 40 tokens.
- Safety/redact layer: run a pre-inference PII scrubber to mask account numbers, SSNs, phone numbers. Maintain a mapping file for audit (hashed id).

Evaluation methodology:
- Offline eval against 1,000 labeled historical claims: compute per-class F1 and summary ROUGE-L; generate confusion matrix and error taxonomy.
- Online A/B (optional after pilot): route 10% of live staging traffic to Redwood-assisted pipeline and measure human accept rate and avg triage time.
- Sampling strategy for human review: stratified by channel and by predicted confidence (low/medium/high).
- Regression detection: maintain a small suite of 50 golden prompts/claims that must pass on each redeploy.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Sensitive PII leak via logs -> Mitigation: strict log filtering + Atlas KMS + explicit egress deny.
- Risk: Model hallucination in summary leading to incorrect routing -> Mitigation: conservative prompt templates + human-in-loop until confidence thresholds exceed 0.9.
- Risk: Burst overload -> Mitigation: autoscaling policy with fallback model variant (smaller, cheaper) and queueing with backpressure signals.
- Risk: Unexpected latency from quantized model on certain sequence lengths -> Mitigation: run model-only latency matrix during Week 2 and tune compilation kernel settings.

Decision points for Atlas (to be resolved by Day 7):
- Production acceptance threshold (human accept rate target for go/no-go).
- Whether to allow any outbound telemetry to Redwood analytics endpoint.
- Target commit for Dedicated capacity vs continued Private pooling.

Immediate next steps (action owners):
- Atlas: share staging VPC peering details + KMS ARN (owner: Jordan Blake) — due EOD Week 0.
- Redwood SE: prepare deployment manifest and smoke-test script (owner: Sasha Nguyen) — due Day 2 Week 1.
- Security sync: Atlas security + Redwood security call to sign off on egress rules (owner: Priya Singh) — schedule Day 1 Week 1.
- Data team (Atlas): provide anonymized sample dataset and schema (owner: Marta Lopez) — due Day 3 Week 1.

Notes to self (SE):
- Keep quantization conservative initially (8-bit) to avoid quality regressions.
- Track model confidence bins and present to Atlas as part of Workshop #2.
- Save reproducible eval script under linked git PR.

Appendix: quick checklist for final acceptance run:
- Run end-to-end ingest -> infer -> SQS -> audit for 10k messages (synthetic + replay)
- Verify audit logs for every message contain request_id, model_version, prompt_hash, redaction_flag
- Run blind human review sample and tabulate acceptance reasons
